title: Tenant residency enforcer with graceful failover and tenant-specific permit/block lists
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a tenant-aware residency enforcement layer that evaluates contractual residency/sovereignty entitlements and enforces routing controls (region selection + tier routing) with deterministic fallback behavior. Support tenant-level permitlists (allow) and blocklists (deny) for outbound egress destinations, and map model variants to residency-safe alternatives. Provide audit logs and rollout flags for gradual enablement.
background: Regulated customers require per-tenant guarantees that inference for specific workloads stays within allowed jurisdictions (primarily EU). Current routing relies on global region heuristics and lacks a clear entitlement evaluation or deterministic fallback for capacity constraints. This causes compliance risk when capacity is tight or when model variants are unavailable in the requested region.
technical_design:
High level components:
- Entitlement evaluator: Reads tenant policy (residency_required, allowed_regions, blocked_regions, permitlist/denylist of egress endpoints) from account metadata service with caching TTL.
- Decision layer middleware: Synchronous policy check for each request that produces a RoutingDecision: allow(route), deny(403), or fallback(route_variant). Decision outputs include policy_id and reason for audit.
- Variant mapper: Maintains model_variant_catalog mapping model -> {region: variant_id, fallback_variants: [quantized_local, lower-capacity, on-prem-proxy, stub-response]}.
- Enforcement hook in router: Applies decision, increments counters, triggers circuit-breaker when fallback rate exceeds thresholds.
- Audit & trace: Emit structured audit event per request (tenant, policy_snapshot_version, decision, selected_route, fallback_reason) to observability pipeline (stack: tracing, logs, EDH).
- Admin controls: Tenant-level feature flag to enable soft-enforcement (warn-only) vs hard-enforcement (deny/fallback).
Implementation notes:
- Design the evaluator to prefer strong consistency for policy changes with a short-time atomic update path and longer cache TTL for reads.
- Policy precedence: explicit tenant blocklist > tenant allowlist > contract residency_required (if true, only allowed_regions) > global defaults.
- Fallback order: region-local variant -> nearest-region with tenant consent -> quantized or lower-cost variant -> on-prem/private-control-plane proxy -> deny with audit.
- Performance: Decision path budget = 2ms p50. Use in-memory LRU cache with background refresh for policy snapshots.
rolling_strategy: Phased rollout: 1) unit tests + canary in staging (soft-enforcement) 2) enable for internal tenants for 1 week, monitor fallback/detect anomalies 3) opt-in for small EU customers 4) enable hard-enforcement for high-compliance customers only after manual verification. Rollback via feature-flag. Enable telemetry dashboards before broader rollout.
test_plan: Unit tests for evaluator ordering and expiry semantics; integration tests with router simulating capacity constraints and checking fallback order; e2e tests exercising permit/block lists, emergency bypass audit path, and on-prem proxy handshake. Load test decision path at 10k req/s with real caching. Add mutation tests for policy update race windows.
metrics: metrics to instrument: policy_evaluations_total (labels: tenant, result), fallback_rate (tenant, model), deny_count, audit_event_emitted, decision_latency_ms_p50_p95, fallback_type_distribution. Alert: fallback_rate > 2% for >5m for high-compliance tenants -> pager. Also create dashboard showing per-tenant fallback and denied requests.
acceptance_criteria: Evaluator returns deterministic decision within 2ms median for cached policies
Fallback chain exercised in integration tests covering all nodes of mapping
Audit event created for every enforced decision and visible in audit stream
Soft-enforcement flag emits warnings but does not deny or route to fallback
Canary tenants show <0.5% unexpected denies after 48h
security_and_privacy_considerations: Policy changes must be timestamped and recorded; emergency bypasses require two-person approval recorded in audit. Do not send raw customer payloads to audit log; only metadata (tenant id, model id, decision code, routing target). Ensure KMS keys used for on-prem proxy handshake are rotated per org policy.
open_questions: Should we expose tenant policy editing in Console or restrict to support/SEs?
What SLA should trigger automatic region fallback vs manual escalation for enterprise contracts?
Do we allow tenants to define fine-grained per-model permitlists or only tenant-global egress allow/deny?
next_steps: Finalize policy JSON schema and API for account-metadata-service
Prototype evaluator using existing policy cache library
Add variant mapping table to model-catalog service and author migration job
Build canary with soft-enforcement for internal tenants
